result:
mitmweb now uses `_mitmproxy_xsrf` for its XSRF cookie instead of `_xsrf`. I haven't run any tests, per your instructions.

- **Backend:** in `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py`, `Application.__init__` now passes `xsrf_cookie_name="_mitmproxy_xsrf"`. The existing `xsrf_cookies=True` and `samesite="Strict"` settings are unchanged.
- **Frontend:** in `web/src/js/utils.ts`, `fetchApi` now reads the `_mitmproxy_xsrf` cookie when setting `X-XSRFToken`.
- **Changelog:** I added a bullet to `CHANGELOG.md`.

A stale HttpOnly `_xsrf` cookie in the browser no longer matters, because neither the server nor the frontend reads that name any more.

I didn't touch any tests, matching the review-feedback notes. I also didn't rebuild the bundled frontend under `mitmproxy/tools/web/static/`, which still reads the old cookie name until the web build is rerun.
